myth: Eldest son of Cronus, who drew the underworld as his share of the cosmos and rules the dead with a stern but fair hand, jealously keeping every soul that enters his realm.
wants: Every soul they meet counted and sent below, and no one ever brought back from the dead without his leave

myth: Son of Zeus and Hera and the god of war's bloodlust and slaughter, loved by few on Olympus and often beaten by cooler heads like Athena.
wants: Blood spilled in his name on every battlefield, and no retreat once a fight is joined

myth: Firstborn of Cronus and keeper of the hearth fire, a quiet virgin goddess who gave up her Olympian throne rather than see the gods quarrel over it.
wants: Guests sheltered, hearths kept burning, and every household honoured before any temple

myth: Goat-legged god of shepherds, flocks, and wild places, whose pipes charm the woods and whose sudden shout gave the world the word panic.
wants: Wild places left untamed, music played in the open air, and travellers frightened off his hills

myth: Winged god of love and desire, son of Aphrodite in later tales and a primal force of creation in older ones, whose arrows make gods and mortals fall helplessly in love.
wants: Lovers brought together against all sense, and his arrows never refused by a target

myth: Winged daughter of Styx who flies over every battle and contest, sided with Zeus against the Titans, and stands at Athena's hand to crown the winners.
wants: Victories won cleanly and dedicated to her, and no contest thrown or abandoned

myth: Son of Apollo raised by the centaur Chiron, a healer so skilled he raised the dead until Zeus struck him down and set him among the stars.
wants: The sick tended without payment, and serpents spared wherever they are found

myth: The twin of Hypnos and the gentle personification of death itself, who comes for each mortal at their appointed hour and is famously tricked by Sisyphus.
wants: No mortal allowed to cheat their appointed hour, and cheaters of death hunted down

myth: Goddess of discord who, uninvited to a wedding, tossed a golden apple marked for the fairest and so set off the quarrel that became the Trojan War.
wants: Quarrels started among allies, and every feast she was not invited to spoiled

myth: The primordial earth itself, mother of the sky, the mountains, and the Titans, who plotted against her own children whenever they grew cruel to hers.
wants: The land kept fertile and unspoiled, and any god who imprisons her children brought low

myth: Youngest Titan who castrated his father Uranus to seize the throne, then swallowed his own children to escape the same fate until Zeus overthrew him.
wants: The thrones of the Olympians undermined, and every hour he spent in Tartarus repaid

myth: Titan queen and mother of the Olympians, who saved the infant Zeus by handing Cronus a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes.
wants: Children protected from their own parents, and mothers given refuge in her mountains

myth: The Titan who shaped humanity from clay and stole fire from the gods to give it to them, and was chained to a mountain for his kindness.
wants: Forbidden knowledge put in mortal hands, and the gods defied when they hoard it

myth: Daughter of Zeus and Hera who poured nectar for the gods until she wed the deified Heracles, and who can restore youth to the old.
wants: The old given back their vigour, and the cupbearer's duty performed with grace

myth: Swift golden-winged messenger of Hera, who travels along the rainbow to carry the words of the gods and the water of the Styx for their oaths.
wants: Messages carried faithfully and fast, and oaths sworn on Styx-water kept

myth: Son of Hypnos and the shaper of dreams, able to take any human form to deliver messages and visions to sleeping mortals.
wants: Dreams recorded and shared, and his messengers never woken before the vision ends

myth: The starry sky and first king of the cosmos, who imprisoned his monstrous children inside Gaia until his son Cronus maimed and deposed him.
wants: The Titans' line punished for their betrayal, and the stars watched over in his name

myth: Titan who led his brothers in war against the Olympians and was sentenced to hold up the sky on his shoulders forever.
wants: Burdens borne without complaint, and a mortal strong enough to take his place for one day

myth: Titaness of divine order, custom, and law, the second wife of Zeus and mother of the Seasons and the Fates, who once spoke the oracle at Delphi.
wants: Customs upheld, assemblies called properly, and the gods' own laws obeyed by the gods

myth: Titaness of memory and mother of the nine Muses by Zeus, whose pool in the underworld lets the dead remember instead of forget.
wants: Histories preserved, poets trained, and her pool drunk instead of Lethe

myth: Titaness who bore Apollo and Artemis on the floating island of Delos after Hera forbade every land on earth to shelter her.
wants: Mothers and outcasts sheltered, and those who mock her children punished

myth: Merman son of Poseidon and Amphitrite who calms or raises the waves by blowing his twisted conch shell.
wants: Lost sailors guided home, and his conch answered when it sounds

myth: Nereid queen of the sea and wife of Poseidon, mother of Triton, who rules the creatures of the deep from her golden palace beneath the waves.
wants: Sea creatures protected, and her court honoured before Poseidon's

myth: The greatest Greek hero, son of Zeus by a mortal woman, who completed twelve impossible labours and was raised to Olympus as a god after his death.
wants: Monsters slain, impossible tasks undertaken, and the weak defended by the strong

myth: Grim ferryman who poles the souls of the dead across the river Styx, refusing passage to any who cannot pay him his coin.
wants: Every passage paid for, and the unburied dead given the coin they need

myth: Shape-changing son of giants who lived among the Aesir, alternately helping and betraying them, until he engineered Baldur's death and was bound to await Ragnarok.
wants: Pranks played on the mighty, bonds broken, and no oath sworn to him taken seriously

myth: Wife of Odin and queen of the Aesir, who knows the fate of all things but never speaks it, and who tried and failed to protect her son Baldur.
wants: Households kept, secrets of fate guarded, and her children protected at any cost

myth: White god who guards the rainbow bridge Bifrost, who needs less sleep than a bird, can hear grass grow, and will sound the horn that begins Ragnarok.
wants: Borders watched day and night, and his horn sounded the moment a threat appears

myth: Vanir god of sunshine, rain, and good harvests, ruler of the elves, who gave away his self-fighting sword for love of the giantess Gerd.
wants: Fields blessed with sun and rain, peace kept at the harvest, and love pursued boldly

myth: Daughter of Loki, half living and half corpse, who rules the cold realm of those who die of sickness and old age and refused to release Baldur.
wants: The dead left in her keeping, and any who escape her halls dragged back

myth: Skaldic god of poetry and eloquence, husband of Idun, with runes carved on his tongue, who welcomes the fallen to Valhalla with verse.
wants: Deeds of the brave remembered in verse, and oaths spoken at his cup kept

myth: Silent son of Odin who will avenge his father at Ragnarok by tearing open Fenrir's jaws with his thick shoe, and who survives into the new world.
wants: Every wrong done to kin avenged, and silence kept until the moment to strike

myth: Son of Odin born for a single purpose, who grew to full strength in one day and killed Hodr to avenge Baldur.
wants: Debts of blood paid quickly, and no grudge carried past its proper end

myth: Stepson of Thor, a god of archery, skiing, and the winter hunt, said to be so fair a warrior that men called on him before single combat.
wants: Duels fought fairly, game hunted in the snow, and his shield-ship honoured

n: Sif - Goddess of the Golden Hair
myth: Wife of Thor whose golden hair Loki sheared as a prank, forcing him to have the dwarves forge her new hair of living gold.
wants: Fields of grain tended, marriages kept faithful, and insults to her repaid with craft

myth: Blind son of Odin, tricked by Loki into throwing the mistletoe dart that killed his brother Baldur, and reconciled with him in the world after Ragnarok.
wants: The blind and the deceived defended, and Loki's tricks exposed

myth: Goddess and valkyrie of healing who sits on the mountain Lyfjaberg, where the sick who climb to her are made whole.
wants: The wounded healed on the battlefield, and her mountain climbed by any who ask her aid

myth: Sea goddess and wife of Aegir who catches sailors in her net and drags them to her hall beneath the waves.
wants: Gold carried by every sailor for her, and the drowned delivered to her hall

myth: Giant of the sea and brewer to the gods, whose hall beneath the waves hosts their great feasts and whose daughters are the waves themselves.
wants: Feasts held for friends and foes alike, and ale brewed in his great cauldron

myth: Maiden who drives the chariot of the sun across the sky, forever chased by the wolf Skoll, who will catch and devour her at Ragnarok.
wants: The sun's path kept clear, and the wolves that hunt her slain

myth: Brother of Sol who guides the moon across the sky and measures the months, pursued by the wolf Hati.
wants: Months counted and nights watched, and children carried off by the moon kept safe

myth: Giantess who is the earth itself and mother of Thor by Odin.
wants: Soil cared for, and strength drawn from the ground never wasted

myth: Goddess who turned her four sons into oxen to plough a huge piece of land out of Sweden, which became the island of Zealand, and who keeps the unmarried dead.
wants: New land claimed by honest labour, and unwed maidens given shelter

myth: Swift son of Odin who rode Sleipnir for nine nights down to Hel to beg for Baldur's return.
wants: Messages carried to impossible places, and errands for the dead undertaken

myth: Quiet companion of Odin who helped make the first humans and gave them reason, later sent to the Vanir as a hostage and found wanting without Mimir's counsel.
wants: Mortals helped to think for themselves, and decisions never forced

myth: Jackal-headed god of embalming and the necropolis, who guides souls through the underworld and weighs their hearts against the feather of Ma'at.
wants: Bodies treated with respect, tombs left unrobbed, and every heart weighed honestly

n: Set - God of Chaos and Storms
myth: Red god of the desert, storms, and foreigners, who murdered his brother Osiris and fought Horus for the throne, yet also defends Ra's barque against Apep each night.
wants: Rivals cut down, the desert feared, and Horus denied the throne

myth: Creator god of Memphis who spoke the world into being from his heart and tongue, and patron of builders, sculptors, and smiths.
wants: Things built to last, craft taught freely, and plans spoken aloud before they are made

myth: Lion-headed goddess of war and plague, the furious Eye of Ra, who nearly wiped out humanity until the gods tricked her into drinking beer dyed red as blood.
wants: Enemies of the throne destroyed, plagues sent and lifted, and her fury quenched only with red offerings

myth: Sister of Isis and Osiris and wife of Set, who mourned and helped restore Osiris and watches over the dead and the coffin.
wants: The dead mourned properly, and the grieving sheltered in her wings

myth: Goddess of truth, justice, and cosmic order, whose feather is weighed against every heart in the Hall of Judgement.
wants: Truth spoken even when it hurts, and the order of the world kept

myth: Hidden god of Thebes whose true nature none can see, who merged with Ra to become Amun-Ra, king of the gods.
wants: His secrets never pried into, and his temples made the greatest in the land

myth: God of the earth whose laughter causes earthquakes, separated from his sister-wife Nut by their father Shu, and father of Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys.
wants: Graves dug deep and crops grown well, and the earth's riches shared out fairly

myth: Sky goddess whose star-covered body arches over the earth, who swallows the sun each evening and gives birth to it each morning.
wants: The dead set among the stars, and the night sky painted on every coffin lid

myth: God of dry air and light who holds the sky goddess Nut apart from the earth god Geb, separating heaven from earth.
wants: The sky held up and things kept in their places

myth: Lion-headed twin and wife of Shu, goddess of moisture and rain, whose anger once took her away to Nubia and left Egypt parched.
wants: Water shared in drought, and offerings made to coax her back when she is angry

myth: Dwarfish, grinning household god who wards off snakes, demons, and bad dreams, and protects mothers in childbirth with dancing and noise.
wants: Homes guarded with song and dance, and children kept safe through the night

myth: God of the annual flooding of the Nile, a plump, bountiful figure who brings the rich silt that feeds all of Egypt.
wants: The flood honoured each year, and no field left unworked after the waters recede

myth: Cobra goddess of Lower Egypt who rears on the pharaoh's crown and spits fire at the king's enemies.
wants: Rightful rulers guarded, and venom turned on usurpers

myth: Falcon-headed war god of Thebes, embodiment of the pharaoh's conquering might, whose sacred bull is the Buchis.
wants: Battles won for rightful kings, and the Buchis bull honoured

myth: Vast serpent of darkness and dissolution who attacks the sun barque every night, seeking to swallow Ra and unmake creation.
wants: The sun stopped forever, creation unravelled, and every name of his enemies erased

myth: Young moon god of Thebes, son of Amun and Mut, who travels the night sky, measures time, and drives out evil spirits.
wants: Hours kept and spirits of illness cast out under his light

myth: Self-created god who rose from the primeval waters at the dawn of time and made the first gods, and who will one day return everything to those waters.
wants: Things begun well and ended completely, and nothing left half-finished
sig: Heart Shard of an Original God

n: Khepri - God of the Rising Sun
myth: Scarab-beetle god who rolls the sun up into the sky each morning, a symbol of daily renewal and self-creation.
wants: Fresh starts made each morning, and the scarab honoured as a sign of return

myth: Hippopotamus goddess with a lion's limbs and a crocodile's tail, fierce protector of pregnant women and newborns.
wants: Mothers and infants guarded from every danger, and the hippo spared

myth: Vulture goddess of Upper Egypt who spreads her wings over the pharaoh as his protector and mother.
wants: Kings protected beneath her wings, and the fallen picked clean and returned to the land

myth: Scorpion goddess who both inflicts and heals venomous stings, and who guards the entrails of the dead.
wants: Stings cured and venom used wisely, and the canopic jars of the dead guarded

myth: Vulture-crowned mother goddess of Thebes, wife of Amun and mother of Khonsu, revered as the mother of the pharaoh himself.
wants: Mothers revered, and the royal line kept strong

myth: The disc of the sun itself, raised by the pharaoh Akhenaten above all other gods as the single source of life, its rays ending in giving hands.
wants: All other gods set aside, and worship given to the light alone

myth: Ancient mother goddess from whom the Tuatha De Danann take their name, linked with rivers, waters, and the fertility of the land.
wants: Her children gathered back together, and rivers honoured as her sacred body

n: Nuada - King of the Tuatha De Danann
myth: First king of the Tuatha De Danann, who lost his arm in battle, ruled again with an arm of silver, and wields a sword no enemy escapes.
wants: Kings judged on their fitness to rule, and the maimed given their chance to rise again

n: Manannan mac Lir - Lord of the Sea
myth: Sea god and ruler of the Otherworld isles, master of illusions and mists, who rides the waves in a chariot and ferries souls beyond.
wants: Hospitality given to strangers, and voyages made to the edge of the known world

myth: Champion and poet of the Tuatha De Danann, strong in arm and tongue, said to have invented the ogham script.
wants: Ogham carved and taught, and challenges answered with both words and fists

myth: King of the Otherworld realm of Annwn, master of a pack of white, red-eared hounds, who once traded places with a mortal prince for a year.
wants: Bargains kept to the letter, and his hounds never denied their quarry

myth: Gaulish goddess of horses, ponies, and mules, protector of cavalry and stables, often shown riding side-saddle among foals.
wants: Horses treated well, stables kept clean, and riders protected on the road

n: Belenus - God of the Bright Sun
myth: Shining Gaulish and British sun god associated with healing springs, whose name survives in the Beltane fires.
wants: Bonfires lit at Beltane, and healing springs kept clean

myth: Celtic thunder god carrying a lightning bolt and a spoked wheel, honoured across Gaul with fearsome sacrifices.
wants: The wheel of the sky kept turning, and storms answered with offerings

n: Aengus - God of Love and Youth
myth: Young god of love and poetry, son of the Dagda and Boann, whose kisses became birds and who followed his dream-love Caer in the shape of a swan.
wants: Lovers helped to find each other, and dreams of love taken seriously

myth: Enchantress who brewed a potion of wisdom in her cauldron for a year and a day, and chased the boy Gwion through many shapes when he stole it.
wants: Potions brewed patiently, and stolen knowledge chased down

myth: Smith of the Tuatha De Danann who forged weapons that never missed, and who hosted the Feast of Age where his ale granted immortality.
wants: Weapons made perfectly in three strokes, and his feast shared with the worthy

myth: Physician of the Tuatha De Danann who made Nuada's silver arm and blessed a well that healed the wounded, but jealously killed his own son for surpassing him.
wants: The wounded healed after battle, and no student allowed to outshine the master

myth: Father of the sea god Manannan and of the children of Lir, whose second wife turned his four children into swans for nine hundred years.
wants: Kin restored and curses broken, and the swans of the lake left unharmed

myth: Goddess of the river Boyne who defied the forbidden Well of Wisdom and was swept away by its waters, becoming the river itself.
wants: Rivers kept free-flowing, and wisdom sought even when forbidden

myth: One-eyed giant king of the Fomorians whose poisonous gaze destroyed armies, killed at last by his own grandson Lugh.
wants: His eye opened upon his enemies, and the grandson's prophecy undone
sig: Fomorian Warlock of the Dark Blood

myth: Otherworld queen who rides a pale horse no rider can catch, falsely accused of killing her son and forced to carry visitors on her back as penance.
wants: The falsely accused vindicated, and her birds' songs heard by the dying

myth: Gaulish god of the tribe and the people, guardian of the community in war and peace.
wants: The tribe defended above all, and no member left behind

myth: Gaulish god carrying a long-handled mallet and a pot, linked with farming, forests, and wine, who strikes good fortune into the world.
wants: Vineyards tended and grain stored, and the mallet struck for good luck

myth: Divine youth, son of the mother goddess Modron, stolen from her at three nights old and held in a prison none could find until Arthur's men freed him.
wants: Prisoners freed and lost children found

myth: Healer of the Tuatha De Danann who catalogued every herb that grew from her murdered brother's grave, until her father scattered them.
wants: Herbs gathered and catalogued, and healing lore never hoarded
